sentences.text: Morrinhosuchus was an extinct notosuchian crocodyliform, a group of ancient crocodile relatives, that lived in Brazil. Its skull and jaws were broad at the rear but narrowed significantly toward the front. The lower jaw also featured a distinct upward arch.
This species possessed seven post-caniniform teeth, a count that distinguishes it from the similar genus Mariliasuchus, which has only six.
The genus name commemorates a nearby hill, while the species name honors a chapel situated on its summit.
Scientists know this animal only from a lower jaw and the front portion of a skull discovered in Monte Alto.
Iori and Carvalho formally described the genus in 2009. They placed it within the family Sphagesauridae and the subfamily Caipirasuchinae.
Researchers hypothesize that Morrinhosuchus hunted Adamantinasuchus, Brasiliguana, and mammals, though this view remains debated as it relies on ecological context rather than direct evidence.
Despite being a predator, it was likely prey for various contemporaries, including Baurusuchus, Campinasuchus, Gondwanasuchus, Pissarrachampsa, Stratiotosuchus, Montealtosuchus, and Pepesuchus.
This creature inhabited the Adamantina Formation during the Campanian to Maastrichtian stages, living between 83.6 and 66 million years ago.
